It does not by itself prove that session +0x28D is the canonical Gate-owner field in all normal, AI-owned, or scripted scenarios. A reverse-owner control is required before promotion to confirmed.

supported_conclusions: Participant pointer-table index 0 is the P1/player object in this capture because its base-G field is 190, matching the displayed player Serpenoid.
Participant pointer-table index 1 is the P2/AI object in this capture because its base-G field is 230, matching the displayed opponent.
Participant index 0 owns Juggernoid ID 19 in this capture because ID 19 is present in its three Gate-card slots and absent from participant index 1's Gate-card slots.
The ordered session pair is +0x28D = 0 and +0x28E = 1 when participant index 0 owns the active Gate and participant index 1 contests it.
The battle constructor uses the same player/AI objects that supply the displayed 190 and 230 base-G values.

verification_requirements: Capture an AI-owned Gate contested by the player and inspect +0x28D/+0x28E at the same constructor boundary.
Require +0x28D = 1 and +0x28E = 0 in that reverse-owner control before naming the fields canonical owner and challenger.
